item.text: {"text":"Multi-negative sampled softmax is a plausible objective change while preserving NextItNet’s causal convolution backbone. [Wu et al., TOIS 2024](https://wujcan.github.io/papers/tois-ssm.pdf) show that sampled softmax implicitly emphasizes hard negatives and connects optimization to ranking quality; temperature controls gradient concentration, with excessively low temperatures allowing a few hard negatives to dominate. Their experiments concern collaborative filtering, so transfer to NextItNet remains a hypothesis. [Prakash et al., 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) compare random, popularity, in-batch, mixed and adaptive sampling for sequential recommendation: performance depends on dataset characteristics, and popularity-based negatives can improve balance across popularity bands while reducing aggregate accuracy.\n\nHardest-negative mining risks penalizing plausible future positives. [UFNRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04116), an earlier relevant study, explicitly identifies potential false negatives and uses teacher-generated soft labels; that teacher–student design should not be imported into this constrained single-model experiment. A practical hypothesis is one NextItNet trained with multi-negative cross-entropy, excluding padding, the target and known training-history positives, then comparing uniform sampling against a modest random/semi-hard mixture selected using the same network. Tune negative count and temperature before aggressive mining; high model scores alone cannot identify false negatives. These are proposed adaptations, not established Electronics improvements. Retain one checkpoint per category and select exclusively through the fixed four-category macro validation HR@10; improved sampled margins or training loss cannot establish recommendation gains."}
